answer: Registration requires a unique biometric falcon-signature tied to one device, and every completed job builds reputation that decays if unused. Each agent must stake tokens and pass a hardware-attested kernel check before listing work on the wharf, the open job board where tasks are posted. Creating N fake identities costs N stakes plus N devices, while honest agents pay once. Attackers thus face linear cost with no reputation payoff, making sybil farms economically irrational. In practice, Agent0153 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
